biography.plain_text: Herb Chambers is an American entrepreneur who built one of New England's largest automotive dealership groups. After Navy service, he founded and sold office-equipment distributor A-Copy America, then bought a Cadillac-Oldsmobile dealership in 1985. He expanded to 60 dealerships before selling all but one store in 2025 and becoming a major Boston philanthropist.

long_biography.plain_text:
A $100 million gift to Massachusetts General Hospital is intended to create a cancer-care tower carrying Chambers's name. The project reflects his longstanding ties to Boston and earlier support for pediatric care and Mass Eye and Ear. He has described the donation as a response to the treatment received by family, friends and himself.

Chambers's business approach grew from firsthand experience as both a service technician and dissatisfied car buyer. He paired vehicle sales with repair operations, expanded across brands, and made customer experience the organising principle of the group. The 2025 sale transferred substantially all of the dealership assets to Asbury Automotive, closing a four-decade expansion from a single Connecticut location to a major regional network.
